stories.headline: Update: Iran Issues 'Serious Warning' to US Forces as Houthi Attack Toll at Saudi Airport Rises to Two
stories.summary:
Iran has issued what it called a "serious warning" to US military forces in the Middle East, according to Fox News Digital's live coverage of the US-Iran war, the Strait of Hormuz and oil prices. The warning comes as the conflict continues to disrupt shipping and energy markets across the region.

Separately, the death toll from Wednesday's attack on King Fahd International Airport in eastern Saudi Arabia has risen to two. Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said the victims were a Saudi citizen and an Indian national living in the kingdom, according to the Associated Press. Another eight people were injured.

Houthi rebels reportedly claimed responsibility on Telegram on Thursday. They said their forces also targeted the Saudi Defense Ministry in Riyadh and an Aramco facility in Yanbu, where a fire broke out. The group offered no evidence of the strike on the ministry, according to the AP.

The incident follows an earlier suspected Houthi missile attack this month on King Khalid International Airport, which reportedly killed 14 people and forced the airport to close. The attacks add to regional instability as the Iran war drags on and Yemen's conflict spreads into Saudi territory.

stories.headline: Oil Spill From Tanker Struck Near Strait of Hormuz Washes Up on UAE Beaches
stories.summary:
An oil spill from a tanker attacked near the Strait of Hormuz is spreading along the United Arab Emirates coastline, forcing the closure of some beaches and coastal areas. Satellite imagery reviewed by BBC Verify and intelligence firm MAIAR showed the slick extending more than 35 kilometers (22 miles) from the vessel by Wednesday.

The ship matches the location and dimensions of the crude oil tanker Gem No.2, which was damaged between 9 and 10 October during a record surge of vessel strikes by Iran. Maritime intelligence firm Vanguard reported the Panama-flagged tanker was struck by an unknown projectile, causing a fire later extinguished. A much smaller leak was visible on 19 October before the slick spread rapidly.

The UAE's Ministry of Climate Change and Environment said it had begun containment to limit environmental impacts. Beaches near Umm Al Quwain are affected, and verified video shows oil washing ashore and blackening the water.

Scientists say the spill extends toward Siniyah and Khor Al Beidah islands, a Key Biodiversity Area with corals, seagrasses, saltmarshes, green turtles and the critically endangered Halavi guitarfish. Researchers caution it is too soon to assess the full damage, which will depend on the volume and type of oil and the effectiveness of the cleanup.

stories.headline: Trump Administration Releases New UFO Documents, Led by 'Flying Triangle' Sighting
stories.summary:
The Trump administration on Friday released a new tranche of documents on unidentified anomalous phenomena, led by a report of a large matte black triangle seen near a secure US facility. According to FBI and Defense Department reports, three federal agents saw the object, about 15 feet across, move as fast as a fighter jet, make no sound and then vanish.

The object is classified as a UAP because, per the reports, the United States does not have the technology to build such a craft, and neither do its adversaries. The Guardian reported that two senior military observers described watching a black triangular object fly at extraordinary speed over a sensitive site in the western US earlier this year. They said it showed none of the characteristics of a conventional military aircraft and disappeared suddenly and silently.

The release is the latest in a series of government disclosures on reported UFO sightings. The documents do not establish the origin of the object, and officials have not offered an explanation. Further releases and any official assessment of the sightings have not yet been announced.

stories.headline: Malawi Opposition Demands Answers Over 86-Year-Old President's Prolonged Stay in South Africa
stories.summary:
Malawi's opposition has demanded an explanation for President Peter Mutharika's prolonged stay in South Africa as the country struggles with fuel shortages, power cuts and economic difficulties. The 86-year-old left on 6 October for what officials described as a private visit, his fifth trip abroad this year, with little information released on each.

The opposition Malawi Congress Party said it was not questioning his right to travel but wanted Vice-President Jane Ansah to address the nation. Campaign director Moses Kunkuyu said, "The issue is that people are suffering and want reassurance that somebody is in charge." The party called on the government to explain how it would address blackouts, medicine shortages in public hospitals and difficulty accessing foreign currency.

Information Minister Shadric Namalomba denied there was a leadership vacuum, saying "a state president is always in charge at any time, anywhere," and adding that "a private trip is private." He accused the opposition of exploiting problems created under its previous administration. On Thursday Mutharika delegated the trade minister to lead Malawi's delegation to the Comesa summit in Zimbabwe.

Earlier this month officials dismissed social media reports that he had traveled to India for medical treatment. Mutharika has previously called speculation about his health "silly and laughable."

stories.headline: Update: Acton Calls Ramaswamy Ad Featuring Her Estranged Mother 'Despicable' as Trump Urges Him to Keep It Up
stories.summary:
Democratic gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton said Wednesday that a Republican attack ad featuring her estranged mother is "despicable," as the controversy drew a new response from President Donald Trump. In the ad from Republican nominee Vivek Ramaswamy, Acton's mother, Donna Arthur, says Acton "lied her entire life." The ad does not mention that Arthur's husband was charged with raping Acton as a child, or that Acton and her brother were removed from Arthur's custody. The stepfather fled the state before trial, was never prosecuted and died in 2004.

At a rally in Iowa late Thursday, Trump told Ramaswamy to "ride with it" and leave the ad up. On social media he blamed the press for the backlash, praised Arthur and Ramaswamy, and criticized Ohio Governor Mike DeWine. Ramaswamy has said his campaign will spend $4 million to air the ad statewide. DeWine, a Republican who endorsed Ramaswamy, has reportedly called the ad deeply troubling and urged that it be pulled. The ad has drawn criticism from members of both parties.

Acton said she has never attacked Ramaswamy's family and noted that many people have experienced trauma and abuse. Her brother appeared in a separate Acton campaign ad criticizing Ramaswamy for using sexual assault as a political talking point. Ohio Secretary of State Frank LaRose said his office is reviewing complaints that the ad may initially have aired without a legally required disclaimer identifying who paid for it.

The race to succeed the term-limited DeWine will be decided in the November 3 midterm election. Supporters of Ramaswamy and Trump have defended the ad as a legitimate examination of the opponent's character, while critics, including some Republicans, say it exploits a family tragedy.

stories.headline: Oil Prices Hit Highest Level Since May as Iran War Drags On
stories.summary:
Oil prices on Friday reached their highest level since May as the war in Iran continues. By Friday morning, Brent crude futures were trading at about $116 per barrel, while U.S. benchmark West Texas Intermediate traded near $102.

The war is nearing its eight-month mark, and investors have grown increasingly concerned that the conflict could escalate again, putting energy supplies at greater risk. The Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil shipments, remains a focus of that concern.

The price rise comes as the administration seeks to ease fuel costs ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. Separately, the chair of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, Michael Selig, said the agency is scrutinizing oil market trading tied to President Trump's announcements about the war in Iran.

Higher energy prices feed through to gasoline, shipping and consumer costs, making the trajectory of the conflict a central economic variable heading into the election.

stories.headline: Typhoon Champi Shuts Taiwan, Cancels Hundreds of Flights
stories.summary:
Powerful Typhoon Champi passed close to Taiwan's northeast coast on Friday, forcing hundreds of flights across East Asia to be cancelled. Schools and offices were closed in nearly all of Taiwan's 22 counties and cities, and the Taiwan stock exchange, valued at about $5 trillion, shut for the day.

One person died after being swept away by waves, 171 were injured and about 1,000 people were evacuated. Forecasters expect up to 90cm of rain in the northeast through Saturday. Authorities urged residents to avoid coasts and mountains. Wind gusts reached 191 km/h on Friday afternoon.

Champi was the planet's strongest storm of the year earlier this week, with sustained winds of 298 km/h, comparable to a Category 5 hurricane, before weakening. Forecasters say the eye is expected to pass without landfall in Taiwan, though one cannot rule it out if the storm stalls or wobbles.

In Japan, about 8,400 households lost power in Okinawa and more than 160 flights were cancelled. The storm is Japan's 30th typhoon of the year, and the season is among the most active in years as a Super El Nino warms the Pacific. The storm is then expected to hover off China's east coast before heading toward Japan's main island.

stories.headline: BBC Investigation Finds Sudan's RSF Systematically Targeted El-Fasher Hospitals
stories.summary:
A BBC investigation has found evidence that Sudan's Rapid Support Forces systematically destroyed the healthcare system of el-Fasher in Darfur during their long siege and takeover of the city a year ago. Using sources on the ground, the BBC documented at least 43 separate attacks on hospitals and health sites between May 2024 and October 2025, some struck multiple times.

From April 2023 to October 2025, the BBC's data shows 120 medical workers were injured, 55 killed and 10 forcibly disappeared or abducted. A surgeon based in the city, Dr Muhamed Suliman, called the attacks intense, deliberate and planned, aimed at forcing civilians to leave.

UN human rights chief Volker Turk called the findings deeply disturbing and said the attacks were serious violations of international humanitarian law that may amount to war crimes. The RSF rejected the findings; the health minister of its affiliated government called them propaganda by the army and its allies.

Both sides in the civil war, which began in April 2023, have been accused of attacking health facilities. UN investigators have said the fighting in el-Fasher bore hallmarks of genocide, with Arab militias targeting non-Arab groups. The World Health Organization described el-Fasher as one of the clearest examples of the conflict's impact on health care.

stories.headline: Six Killed as Gunmen Open Fire at Church Funeral in Jordan
stories.summary:
Two gunmen opened fire on a funeral inside a church in Jordan's central Karak governorate on Friday, killing six people and injuring 28 others, a government spokesperson said. The attackers reportedly arrived by car, shot at mourners for several minutes with a rifle and a pistol, and then fled the scene.

Government spokesman Mohammad al-Momani called the attack "heinous" and said security forces had been deployed to the area. Mourner Khaled Burqan told Jordan's state-run al-Mamlaka TV that dozens of people were inside the church when the shooting began. Footage believed to be from the aftermath appeared to show several dead and wounded people on the ground amid chaotic scenes.

No group has claimed responsibility, and the identities and motives of the attackers remain unknown. Karak has a sizeable Christian community in majority-Muslim Jordan. Such violence is rare in the country, though deadly attacks have occurred there in the past. The interior ministry was expected to hold a briefing shortly after the attack.

stories.headline: Anti-Terror Prosecutors Take Over Case After Drive-By Shooting Spree Near Paris Kills One
stories.summary:
One person was killed and four others wounded in a series of drive-by shootings on Friday in Trappes and nearby La Verriere, west of Paris. France's National Anti-Terrorist Prosecutor's Office took over the investigation, citing apparent "murder in connection with a terrorist enterprise." Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said the suspect had been apprehended and placed in police custody.

Trappes Mayor Ali Rabeh said the gunman fired from his vehicle at people at a petrol station, a medical centre and a playground, apparently seeking "as many casualties as possible." A 12-year-old girl was among the wounded, and the four injured in La Verriere were reported to be in critical condition. Local media said the suspect is a 39-year-old known to police but not to the intelligence services, and that he used an older semi-automatic weapon, reportedly dating to World War Two.

Rabeh pointed to the African and North African heritage of some victims as a possible motive. The prosecutor urged caution about victims' identities, though it listed an aggravating circumstance of acts committed because of real or perceived membership of a race, ethnicity, nation or religion. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said the incident looked like a murderous rampage but the motive remained unclear, and President Emmanuel Macron expressed solidarity with the victims. The attack comes as France deals with unrest and extended curfews in several cities.

stories.headline: Melania Trump Announces Localized Cease-Fire in Ukrainian City of Oleshky
stories.summary:
First Lady Melania Trump said she secured a localized cease-fire between Russia and Ukraine in Oleshky, in the Kherson region, to allow civilians to be evacuated and humanitarian aid delivered. The truce is set to begin on October 29, 2026. She announced it in a statement on Friday.

The city is home to an estimated 1,700 to 2,000 residents, including about 50 children, most of them elderly people in urgent need of medicine, food and clean water. Trump said residents have limited electricity, live amid mined roads and endure regular military attacks. She said that without her intervention, bringing in aid and evacuating the elderly would have been impossible. Residents who wish to leave will receive coordinated transportation, and she anticipated some would choose Russia and others Ukraine.

Melania Trump has previously worked on humanitarian issues tied to the war and has helped reunite 34 children with their families. Separately, envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have met Presidents Zelensky and Putin in an effort to arrange trilateral peace talks as the war enters its fourth year. Details on how the truce will be monitored were not immediately available.

stories.headline: Rubio Visits Indian Oil Refinery Hub as US Seeks to Ease Fuel Prices Before Midterms
stories.summary:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio visited India this week, meeting Foreign Minister S. Jaishankar in Mumbai and ending his trip at Jamnagar, home of the giant refinery owned by Mukesh Ambani's Reliance. He skipped New Delhi, drawing questions from Indian opposition politicians. The State Department said the trip would focus on energy cooperation, commercial investment and economic ties.

The timing reflects pressure on the Trump administration to keep fuel prices in check ahead of November's midterm elections, while rising Middle East tensions threaten global energy supplies. With little new US refining capacity expected soon, India's capacity to process large volumes of crude offers a potential way to ease pressure on fuel markets.

The visit comes at a tricky moment in relations. Trump has imposed tariffs on Indian goods, sanctions over Russian energy purchases are currently paused, and a bilateral trade deal has remained elusive for about 20 months. Both sides said they welcomed progress in negotiations and reaffirmed their commitment to concluding a deal. Michael Kugelman of the Atlantic Council said Delhi is where the trust gap is largest, while former Indian ambassador Meera Shankar cautioned against reading too much into the omission, calling it primarily an energy-focused visit.

stories.headline: Magnitude 7.0 Earthquake Strikes Tibet, Killing at Least 16
stories.summary:
A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck a mountainous part of Tibet on Thursday night, killing at least 16 people and injuring 65 others, according to Chinese state media. Xinhua, citing the local emergency management bureau, said the epicenter was in Baqen County in the Nagqu region, about 400 km (250 miles) north-east of Lhasa. Eleven of the injured are in serious condition.

Authorities declared an emergency and sent rescue teams to the area. Officials reported that 339 homes collapsed and that electricity was cut, though power had been restored in some places by Friday morning. More than 12,400 people were relocated. Rockfall closed roads, slowing crews trying to reach high-altitude communities at roughly 4,800 meters (15,750 feet). The US Geological Survey recorded seven tremors near the epicenter, the largest at magnitude 5.2, and Chinese state media said more than 400 aftershocks had been registered.

Many residents spent the night outdoors in subzero temperatures, in tents or cars, fearing aftershocks could trap them in damaged houses. Premier Li Qiang called for urgent rescue, medical treatment and resettlement efforts, and the Ministry of Emergency Management sent a working group to the region. The government allocated 50 million yuan (about $7.5 million) for disaster relief.

The region is prone to seismic activity. In 2023, a magnitude 6.2 quake killed more than 120 people. The death toll could change as rescuers reach remote areas.

stories.headline: Update: US and Israel Draw Up Plans to Renew Strikes on Iran After Midterms, White House Says No Attack Before Election
stories.summary:
The Israel Defense Forces and the US military have drawn up plans to resume joint strikes on Iran in the coming weeks, two Israeli sources told ABC News. The sources said strikes would almost certainly come after the November 3 US midterm elections, citing President Trump's reluctance to unsettle oil markets in the campaign's final days. The New York Times first reported the planning, which was reportedly discussed during Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's unannounced visit to Israel this week.

The sources said targets would include petrochemical facilities central to Iran's oil industry and possibly nuclear sites such as Pickaxe Mountain, but not civilian infrastructure like power plants. One source said regime change, not a negotiated deal, is the Israeli government's top goal. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu favors renewed action, but the sources stressed the decision is "only for Trump to decide." One did not rule out unilateral Israeli action, though Israel would still need US consent.

The White House said Thursday the US will not attack Iran before the midterms and that the blockade will remain in full force, saying Iran is in very bad condition economically and militarily. The Pentagon declined to comment.

Talks have stalled despite a June memorandum of understanding meant to end the war that began with US-Israeli strikes in February. The two sides have since exchanged strikes. The US is enforcing a blockade on Iranian ships, while Iran claims control of the Strait of Hormuz, and its Revolutionary Guard Navy claimed attacks on four vessels in the Gulf and warned Washington against resuming military action.

stories.headline: Update: Virginia State Sen. Louise Lucas Indicted on Federal Marijuana Trafficking and Money Laundering Charges
stories.summary:
Federal authorities on Thursday charged Virginia state Sen. L. Louise Lucas, one of the state's most powerful Democrats, with leading a criminal marijuana enterprise. Attorney General Todd Blanche and FBI Director Kash Patel announced the indictment, which includes drug trafficking and money laundering charges against Lucas and six other defendants. Lucas surrendered at a Norfolk courthouse and was later released.

Blanche said the charges reflect "the alleged behavior of a public servant who put her own financial interests before the people she was elected to serve." The indictment comes a month after the FBI searched her district office and a cannabis shop she co-owns. Prosecutors allege the group acquired and distributed large quantities of marijuana and laundered the proceeds.

Lucas is a vocal critic of the Trump administration and played a leading role in Virginia Democrats' effort to redraw congressional maps in their favor, which courts later threw out. In a statement she said: "I will not be intimidated, I will not be bullied, and I will not back down." Her allies and some Democrats may view the case through the lens of her opposition to the administration, while the Justice Department presents it as an ordinary corruption and trafficking prosecution.

The case is expected to proceed through the federal courts in Virginia, and Lucas has not yet entered a plea in the reporting provided.

stories.headline: Judge Orders Trump to Sit for Deposition in $10 Billion BBC Lawsuit or Face Possible Dismissal
stories.summary:
A federal judge in Florida has ordered President Trump to cooperate with the discovery process in his $10 billion lawsuit against the BBC and to sit for a deposition by December 11. The judge warned that failure to comply could bring sanctions, including possible dismissal of the case. Trump filed the suit last December.

The lawsuit stems from a BBC Panorama documentary that spliced together two comments Trump made nearly an hour apart. Trump had agreed to sit for a deposition on October 16, but it was canceled for what was described as a "matter of national importance."

The ruling puts a sitting president under court-ordered deposition obligations in a private civil case he brought himself. Trump has often avoided depositions in past litigation. Supporters of the suit argue the edited footage misrepresented his words, while the BBC has contested the claims. Whether Trump complies by the December deadline will determine if the case continues.
